findings.english_quote: Bounded Athos and Latin alternatives are separately disclosed in reader notes.
findings.issue: The theological metadata claims disclosure of Athos alternatives, but the supplied reader notes identify only Latin alternatives. They identify neither an Athos reading nor any conjecture report. This is a concrete mismatch between the claimed disclosure and the supplied notes; it does not establish that the quoted Greek clause, or any other particular clause, is an Athos variant or editorial supplement.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove the unsupported claim that Athos alternatives are disclosed, or supply the relevant apparatus evidence and add a bounded note identifying the actual reading and its status. Where the evidence identifies conjectural or editorially supplied wording, distinguish that status from preserved witness text. Retain the selected working reading unless further review establishes a reason to change it.

findings.source_quote: ὅτι ἐὰν ἐπιστραφῆτε πρὸς τὸν Κύριον ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας ὑμῶν καὶ ἐργάσησθε τὴν δικαιοσύνην τὰς λοιπὰς ἡμέρας τῆς ζωῆς ὑμῶν καὶ δουλεύσητε αὐτῷ ὀρθῶς κατὰ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ, ποιήσει ἴασιν τοῖς προτέροις ὑμῶν ἁμαρτήμασι, καὶ ἕξετε δύναμιν τοῦ κατακυριεῦσαι τῶν ἔργων τοῦ διαβόλου.
findings.english_quote: If you turn back to the Lord with your whole heart, do righteousness for the rest of your life[d], and serve him rightly according to his will, he will bring healing[e] for your former transgressions. You will have power to master the devil’s works.
findings.issue: The separate, unqualified sentence about receiving power detaches that promise from the preceding conditions. In the Greek, healing and receiving power are coordinated consequences within the same conditional construction. The standard edition preserves this connection; the simplified edition does not explicitly preserve it.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “If you turn back to the Lord with your whole heart, do righteousness for the rest of your life[d], and serve him rightly according to his will, he will bring healing[e] for your former transgressions, and you will have power to master the devil’s works.” Alternatively, retain shorter sentences while explicitly carrying the same conditions into the second promise.

findings.english_quote: Bounded Athos and Latin alternatives are separately disclosed in reader notes.
findings.issue: Independently checked, the simplified edition's metadata makes the same unsupported disclosure claim: its supplied reader notes identify Latin alternatives but no Athos alternative or conjecture report. The supplied material does not establish which selected clause, if any, has that particular apparatus status.
findings.suggested_revision: Correct the metadata to describe the disclosures actually supplied, or provide the relevant apparatus evidence and an accurately scoped reader note. Distinguish any evidenced editorial supplement or conjecture from preserved text without replacing the disclosed working reading merely because an alternative exists.

summary: Both editions were checked clause by clause against the supplied working Greek. The standard reader text preserves the assertions, conditions, negations, dialogue, and contextual repentance terminology. The simplified text needs an explicit connection between the conditions and the promise of power. Both editions also need correction or substantiation of their claimed Athos disclosure. The Latin reports and source-restoration history remain supplied editorial reports, not independently verified witness evidence. These findings do not certify unseen editions, handwriting, or exhaustive collation; proposed wording requires fresh review.
